programmes.d: Time of death becomes pivotal after a pregnant woman is found murdered in her air-conditioned bedroom. A striking similarity between her death and an HBO movie gives examiners the clues they need to thaw out the alibi of a cold-blooded killer.
In 2000, construction manager Darrell North was found dead in his work trailer in Ft. Worth, Texas.
In this episode, the decade-old murder of a young Texas housewife is investigated.
In 2000, Judy Southern arrived home from work and was shot by a gunman waiting within.

They thought the fire would cover their crime. But one tiny clue, no bigger than a thumbtack, remained. It held all the information investigators needed to put a trio of cold-blooded killers behind bars.
In 1986, Gary Dale Larson was stabbed to death in his Edmond, Oklahoma home.

A beautiful young woman falls to her death from a cliff overlooking the ocean. Initially, investigators think it was a tragic accident. But after a forensic examination, police uncover a very different picture of what happened.
In 1991, Dorothy Donovan was murdered in her Dover, Delaware home.
In 2001, Ginger Hayes and her infant son Nicholas were abducted during a carjacking.
In 2003, Kathy Lorick was murdered on a Concord, California jogging trail while talking to her husband on her mobile phone.
New clues are found in the form of a phone and shoes in a rape and murder case unsolved for 8 years.

Alaskan hikers discover a body wrapped in sheets which were edged in orange stitching. Investigators find a tuft of red carpet fibers clinging to the sheet — threads of evidence which lead them straight to the killer.
A nosy neighbor with a disturbing obsession becomes a suspect in a woman's murder.
A young woman attends evening church services, then disappears. When her abandoned car is found, the tank is empty and a gas can she kept in her trunk for emergencies is missing.
Blood splatter is found in the bedroom of a missing girl's boyfriend.
In 1995, Palm Beach waitress Denise O'Neill is abducted and murdered. Her neighbor Luis Caballero arouses suspicions by behaving oddly toward TV crews covering the crime.
A serial rapist is on the loose in a Texas town and no one knows where he'll strike next.

The murders of an elderly couple leave police stumped until, two years later, they receive a major break. A jeweler looking through old newspaper clippings recognizes a necklace the female victim wore as having been pawned in her own shop.
The victim has been stabbed more than thirty times, and the crime scene is awash with her blood.
In 1989, the dead bodies of Joan Rogers and her two teenage daughters were found floating in Tampa Bay.
A young woman attends evening church services... then disappears.
One warm summer afternoon, the town of Verona, Wisconsin faced its first triple homicide. To solve the case, investigators had to delve into the world of high rollers and offshore betting.
When a nine-year-old girl goes missing, police and volunteers spend weeks searching for her.

In the search for the killer of two Texas teenagers, a behavioral profile led to suspect Jason Massey. Hard science proved the profile was correct, and Massey was executed by lethal injection on April 3, 2001.
Digital enhancement of security camera video shows that what appears to be a forced abduction.

In 2000, construction manager Darrell North was found dead in his work trailer in Ft. Worth, Texas. When investigators arrived, they found that he had been stabbed 46 times, indicating a personal relationship between the victim and the attacker.
The woman had been sexually assaulted, stabbed repeatedly, and left for dead.
In 1998, a Maryland murder mystery performance turns into a real whodunit when the badly burned body of Stephen Hricko is discovered in his hotel room.
When a businessman is murdered, the motive may be a disgruntled employee, client, or racy photos.

While vacationing in California, Earl Morris learns that his wife has gone missing from their Arizona home. The search for Ruby Morris involves dozens of investigators and scientists — and even the Coast Guard.
A family vacation turns into a nightmare when the wife is found face-down in the lake.
The woman in the back of the truck was flailing her arms, screaming.

One investigator's quick thinking helps him capture a shoe impression made in snow before the evidence melts away. The shoe leads investigators to Peter Benedict and Frank Lanoue, who are convicted of aggravated assault and robbery.
When court clerk Peter Porco doesn't report to his work, a courts officer is ordered to his home.
Who was the sexual offender who murdered two adolescent boys in Nebraska? The key to stopping him would be the unique composition of the "junk rope" he used to tie his victims.
Two suspects are linked to a murder by bloodstained boots and a gun.

In 1991, a high school girl vanished after attending a party. The prime suspect had two alibi witnesses for the night she disappeared. A solid alibi can often overcome circumstantial evidence, but forensic evidence is another matter.
This episode documents a deadly bombing at a church in Oakwood, Illinois, in December 1997.

Shortly after daybreak, a fire is started in a dumpster in Vancouver. No one sees the arsonist or the fire, which burns for hours in the deserted parking lot. But there's more than garbage in this flaming container.
There was no clear reason for a young, healthy college student to be dead.

6-year-old Nicole Rae Walker was killed in a hit-and-run in her Ft. Lauderdale neighborhood. The prosecutor combines the talents of an accident reconstruction expert with a video specialist to create a graphic demonstration of the moment of impact.
A young woman is stabbed more than 100 times and the killer leaves DNA behind.
On the night of May 22, 1992, Betty Wilson returned home after a meeting and discovered her husband lying in a pool of blood. Jack Wilson had obviously been murdered — but how?
On Christmas eve 2005, the corpse of a black male is found burning near Baltimore.
In 1987, a human skull and some bones were discovered at a Boy Scout Camp near Farmington, Missouri. Facial reconstruction aids the investigators in this case.
Forensics study a strand of a murdered man's hair to reveal a record of his last six months alive.
At the scene of a vicious murder, the killer went to a great deal of effort to wipe away his fingerprints and obscure his shoe impressions left when he tracked blood trails on the floor.
A bullet-riddled car, a missing driver, and no witnesses. Was this an ambush or a random attack?

Two suspects are linked to a murder by bloodstained boots and a gun, but the owner of the items says he has never met the victim. Investigators hope manufacturing codes from beer bottles will determine who is telling the truth.
Even though their daughter had run away before, she'd always come back.
It's usually easy to determine how a criminal entered the crime scene. But in this case, it looked as if the killer vanished into thin air — and perhaps he had.
Serial killer who hates women, brutally murdered two women who lived in the same apartment complex.

A go-go dancer told her family she needed to get away for a while and then she simply disappeared. Investigators were suspicious, because she took neither her car nor her clothes. 20 years later, her family received a call that changed everything.
When a college co-ed vanished without a trace, her fellow students were concerned about her safety.

An investigation of a pediatrician, prompted by the mysterious death of one of her patients, leads to a Texas hospital where the pediatric mortality rate is higher than at any hospital in the country.
Moments before she dies, a woman writes a name on a wall with her blood.
An assistant manager of a Florida steakhouse is stabbed to death.

When a young woman disappeared, police feared she was the latest victim in a string of similar crimes. A pair of bloody gloves, unique tire tracks and ordinary pine needles provided investigators with some extraordinary clues.
A convenience store safe was empty and the clerk's naked body was found at a nearby woods.
A 34-year-old nurse experiences a variety of flu-like symptoms. None of her doctors are able to discover the cause, until she visits her gynecologist for a routine check-up.
Tracey Frame, 35, was convicted of killing David Nixon after he planned to end their relationship.

Bombings are difficult to solve because the perpetrator isn't usually at the scene and the evidence goes up in smoke. In this case, pieces of plastic the size of grains of sand hold the key to finding a murderer.
Respected surgeon is stabbed to death. However the key suspect has a solid alibi.
When a college student vanished without a trace, her fellow students were concerned about her safety and their own.
A killer made great effort to obscure the shoe impressions left when he tracked blood on the floor.

A millionaire and his family were executed in their own home. For three years, the murders went unsolved. Finally, a 30-year-old box of ammunition and some fluorescent fibers revealed the ultimate betrayal.
In 2007, Brian & Beverly Mauck were found dead in their Graham, Washington home.

A two-man shrimp boat sinks when a fast-moving, violent storm strikes the Louisiana coast. The captain drowns, but the deckhand is rescued fourteen hours later. The crewman is hailed as a hero — until the captain's body is discovered.
On May 12, 1994, Crystal Perry was viciously murdered in her home in Bridgton, Maine.
After a street fight takes the life of a national wrestling champion, police must determine if he was killed in cold blood or in self-defense.
Rachael Mullenix, 19, was convicted of stabbing her mother, Barbara Mullenix.
On May 20, 2001, Carrie Nelson, then 20, was beaten to death while working alone in a park office.
In 1969, 25-year-old phone operator Diane Maxwell was raped and murdered. Her brother promised he'd find out who was responsible and bring the killer to justice.
Foul play is suspected when Fort Worth factory worker Glenda Furch disappears after her shift.

A woman disappears without a trace. Even though foul play is suspected, the leads don't pan out and the trail turns cold. Twenty years would pass before police are able to link a clump of hair discovered in an isolated area with the missing woman.
A week after a couple disappears from the beach, police get a mysterious lead from a robbery.

In 1991, Maine resident Pearl Smith goes missing after an argument with her husband, Bill Bruns. When investigators find a blood trail that leads to the couple's basement, police are sure they'll find the victim's body.
The decade-old murder of a young Texas housewife is investigated.
When a car was found in a drainage ditch with two bodies inside, a fingertip torn from a latex glove would point investigators to both the crime scene and the killer.
In 1995, Palm Beach waitress Denise O'Neill is abducted and murdered.
Police investigate a missing college girl and discover her double life: attending school by day and working as a call-girl by night. Her body is found and investigators find her killer.
In 2007, Shamaia Smith disappeared from the strip club she worked at in East Hartford, CT.
When a dedicated, well-respected teacher disappeared, police had to determine if she'd gone on vacation without telling anyone or if she was the victim of foul play.
A hamburger bun provides the key to solving the case of a young woman murdered in her bathtub.

A wealthy man and his wife were attacked by three masked men outside their luxurious Louisiana home. He was shot dead and she was forced to open their hidden safe. To solve the crime, police would have to find out who knew about the concealed safe.
In 2006, Darlene VanderGiesen received threatening emails and then disappeared.

A young man was killed in a mysterious car crash, but the evidence at the scene led investigators to believe it was not an accident. Forensic science revealed what really happened and the truth devastated three families.
In 2000, Kristine Fitzhugh failed to show up for her music class and her husband Ken found her dead.

A drive-by shooting leaves one man dead and another seriously wounded. Cell phone calls and shell casings point to a suspect, but authorities are unable to place him at the crime scene. A forensic geologist proves that dirt is anything but dumb.
In 1999, Susan Fassett was gunned down as she left church choir practice in Poughkeepsie, NY.

Edward Post drew a bath for his wife before going for a run. He returned to find her not breathing. She died before emergency response arrived. Police considered her death accidental until a motive surfaced.
After a man dies in a fire, his death is ruled an accident until forensic science is used.

The woman was dead. The man had been shot four times and survived. When the man's version of events contradicted physical evidence, investigators turned to forensic science to paint a clearer picture of the crime.
Lack of evidence compels investigators to look beyond the obvious when a woman is beaten to death.
A mother of two vanishes after a shopping trip. Her body is discovered a month later, and witnesses say they saw the victim being forced into a car by an unknown person.
In 2005, David Castor suffered a slow, agonizing death over a period of days.
A dismembered body is dumped on the side of the New Jersey Turnpike.
While investigating the murder of 9-year-old Jessica Knott, police use a garbage bag to connect suspect James Edward Crow, Jr. to the crime.
A young bride-to-be is gunned down and investigators uncover the man she loved was living a lie.

When four-month-old Ryan Stallings dies under suspicious circumstances, his mother is ultimately convicted of his murder. But months later, new evidence emerges from a startling source — his newborn brother.
Tara Munsey went missing after a work shift at a Virginia restaurant.

When a decomposed body is found stuffed in a barrel, it's easy to presume murder. But the body had been placed in the barrel 30 years earlier. One of the few clues was an address book found along with the body.
